_: Shared editorial for the three Blade Polos. Merged UNDER each polo's own file.
_specs: Fabric, fit, weight, features and care are verbatim from the copy skill's Product Reference Guide (The Blade Polo) — identical to the Classic. The collar is the difference. Body measurements are not published and are not invented.
_voice: The reference guide is explicit that apparel does NOT get the clubs' value-comparison framing. No middlemen-and-markups argument on any polo page.

four.v: Light enough for a hot round

fabric.v: Four-way, so it moves in every direction the swing does.

fitParas: Tailored athletic, and the same block as the Classic. If you know your size in one, it is your size in the other.
The blade collar has no buttons and no placket, so the neckline lies flat instead of gapping. It reads a little more fitted at the shoulders for that reason alone; the body has not changed.
Between sizes, or want room across the chest? Size up. Returns are thirty days, unworn with the tags on.
closeBody: $67 in every size, four-way stretch, UPF 50+. Thirty days to send it back unworn if the fit isn't right.

_piece: Cole 2026-07-31: ONE section that works for any design. Every colorway used to carry its own bespoke headline and two paragraphs, which is 22 pages of copy saying the same thing 22 ways. What differs between designs is the photograph, not the garment. Anything genuinely specific to one design goes in that product's own file and overrides these keys.
pieceHeadline: A sharper collar, and the same shirt underneath.
pieceParas: The Blade swaps the traditional collar for a blade collar, which sits flatter and holds its shape without a placket fighting it. Everything below the neck is the Classic: tailored athletic through the body, 88/12 poly-spandex, four-way stretch.
UPF 50+, moisture-wicking, wrinkle-resistant. It reads a little more modern than the Classic and it wears exactly the same, so the choice is the collar and the print. Nothing else changes.
